title: Pairs
experiment: The pair flux quantum h/2e (Deaver–Fairbank, Doll–Näbauer, 1961)
intro: Two particles on the same ring. As in 8-1 the square is the pair: across is particle 1, down is particle 2, and with portals on all four sides the plane is a torus. The flux threads the ring, so it acts on both. The target is a thin line in their total momentum, K = k₁ + k₂, halfway between allowed values. In 9-3 half a flux quantum did it for one particle. Find the flux that does it for two.
goal: Measure the pair's total momentum k₁ + k₂ on the thin green line (1.49). Particle 1 is launched with the speed you choose, particle 2 at rest; choose the flux Φ through the ring.

physics.point: Each particle's momenta move by Φ/Φ₀ of a tooth, so their sum moves twice as fast: for the pair a quarter flux quantum is half a tooth, and the pair's spectrum repeats every half flux quantum, h/2e.

idea: In 1961 Deaver and Fairbank, and independently Doll and Näbauer, measured the flux trapped in tiny superconducting cylinders. It came in steps of h/2e, half the flux quantum h/e that a single electron would need. The charge carriers in a superconductor are pairs of electrons, Cooper pairs, and a pair feels the Aharonov–Bohm phase twice.

This level shows the bookkeeping behind it, without the superconductor. One particle on a ring has momenta k = (2πn + θ)/L (9-3). Two particles each pick up the phase θ per lap, so their total momentum K = (2π(n₁ + n₂) + 2θ)/L: the comb of totals has the same spacing but moves twice as fast with the flux.
So the flux that put one particle on the line in 9-3, half a quantum, moves the pair's comb by a whole tooth: nothing changes. A quarter quantum does it.
maths: With θ = 2πΦ/Φ₀ on both axes of the torus, the allowed (k₁, k₂) are a square grid shifted by (θ/L, θ/L). The totals K = k₁ + k₂ lie on lines of slope −1 in the momentum view, spaced 2π/L ≈ 0.157 in K and shifted by 2θ/L.

The target is the strip K = 9.5 · 2π/40 ≈ 1.492 of half-width 0.03 (drawn as a thin diagonal line). Particle 1 at speed 1.49 and particle 2 at rest, each with a momentum spread 0.1, give a spread in K of 0.14, so one line of totals carries about 41% of the probability:
The particles here do not interact, so this is only kinematics. In a superconductor the pairs are bound, and then the ring's whole spectrum, not only the total momentum, repeats every h/2e.
try: Flux 0.5, the answer to 9-3: P_T is 0. The pair's comb has moved by exactly one tooth.
Flux 0.25: one line of totals sits on the target.
Switch to the momentum view during setup and change the flux: the grid of (k₁, k₂) slides along the diagonal.
